working_account.text: Task: Backport a configparser error improvement. When allow_no_value=True and a valueless option is followed by a continuation line (indented line), reading currently raises an internal AttributeError. Need to reject this with a public MultilineContinuationError derived from ParsingError, with source/lineno/line attributes (one-based line number and exact offending line through source), preserving those three constructor args for pickling/copy, and a useful message. Consistent through read(), read_file(), read_string() for ConfigParser and RawConfigParser. Preserve existing valid multiline values, valueless options, comment handling, constructor modes. Add regressions to existing test module, update reference documentation. Keep existing tests intact. Added regressions must pass with repaired module and fail with original. candidate_id f32256765ff11d4a353900e33ec9b503255cd4718ea344f77e17311a84391170

class MultilineContinuationError(ParsingError):
    """Raised when a continuation line follows a valueless option."""

    def __init__(self, source, lineno, line):
        Error.__init__(
            self,
            'Continuation line found for a valueless option.\nfile: %r, line: %d\n%r' %
            (source, lineno, line))
        self.source = source
        self.lineno = lineno
        self.line = line
        self.args = (source, lineno, line)

class MultilineContinuationErrorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Tests for MultilineContinuationError raised on continuation after valueless option."""

    INPUT = "[service]\noptional_flag\n    continuation\n"

    def test_error_raised_read_string(self):
        parser = configparser.ConfigParser(allow_no_value=True)
        with self.assertRaises(
                configparser.MultilineContinuationError) as cm:
            parser.read_string(self.INPUT)
        self.assertEqual(cm.exception.lineno, 3)
        self.assertEqual(cm.exception.line, '    continuation')

    def test_error_raised_raw(self):
        parser = configparser.RawConfigParser(allow_no_value=True)
        with self.assertRaises(configparser.MultilineContinuationError):
            parser.read_string(self.INPUT)

    def test_error_is_parsing_error(self):
        self.assertTrue(issubclass(
            configparser.MultilineContinuationError,
            configparser.ParsingError))

    def test_error_has_source_attribute(self):
        parser = configparser.ConfigParser(allow_no_value=True)
        with self.assertRaises(
                configparser.MultilineContinuationError) as cm:
            parser.read_string(self.INPUT)
        self.assertIsInstance(cm.exception.source, str)

    def test_valid_multiline_value_still_works(self):
        parser = configparser.ConfigParser(allow_no_value=True)
        text = "[sec]\nkey = first line\n    second line\n"
        parser.read_string(text)
        self.assertEqual(parser.get('sec', 'key'), 'first line second line')

    def test_valueless_option_no_continuation(self):
        parser = configparser.ConfigParser(allow_no_value=True)
        parser.read_string("[sec]\nflag\n")
        self.assertTrue(parser.has_option('sec', 'flag'))

    def test_read_file_raises(self):
        parser = configparser.ConfigParser(allow_no_value=True)
        fd, fname = os_helper.mkstemp()
        try:
            with open(fname, 'w') as f:
                f.write(self.INPUT)
            with self.assertRaises(configparser.MultilineContinuationError):
                parser.read(fname)
        finally:
            os.unlink(fname)

action.new:
removed.  They have been available using the name ``source`` since 3.2.


.. exception:: MultilineContinuationError

   Exception raised when a continuation line (a line beginning with
   whitespace) follows an option that has no value.  This condition is
   only possible when :attr:`!allow_no_value` is ``True``.  Subclass of
   :exc:`ParsingError`.

   Instances provide the following attributes:

   ``source``
      The name of the file or string source being parsed.

   ``lineno``
      The one-based line number of the offending continuation line.

   ``line``
      The exact content of the offending continuation line.
